Here, n = 3.

Now, using formula: (n - 2)² × 6

⇒ (n - 2)2 × 6

⇒ (3 - 2)2 × 6

⇒ 12 × 6

⇒ 1 × 6 = 6.

So, total '6' cubes will have only one face painted.

Hence, the correct answer is **"6"**.

questions.question: Hawa Mahal is situated in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Location and Design:** Hawa Mahal, also known as the "Palace of Winds," is located in Jaipur, the capital city of Rajasthan, India.

 
 
• It was designed in the form of the crown of Lord Krishna, with its unique five-story exterior resembling a honeycomb.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance: **Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, Hawa Mahal is an architectural marvel that is an integral part of Jaipur's history and royal heritage.
 
 
• It was constructed to enable ladies of the royal household to watch the life and processions of the city without being seen from the outside, given the strict "purdah" system followed at that time.
 
 
 
• **Architecture:** Hawa Mahal is a prime example of Rajput architecture and Indian artistry with its pink sandstone construction.
 
 
• The building does not have a foundation, and it is the tallest building in the world that does not have a solid base. It has over 950 windows, known as 'Jharokhas,' decorated with intricate latticework.
 
 
 
• **Ventilation: **The name "Hawa Mahal" translates to "Palace of Winds," which refers to the natural ventilation system in the building.
 
 
• The unique design of the windows allows cool air to circulate naturally through the building, making it an early example of sustainable architecture.
 
 
 
• **Tourism: **Today, Hawa Mahal is one of the most popular tourist attractions in Jaipur. Visitors can climb to the top floor for a panoramic view of the city, including the Jantar Mantar and the City Palace on one side and the Siredeori Bazaar on the other.
 
 
• It's a great place to learn about the culture and history of Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:** The Hawa Mahal is maintained by the Archaeological Department of the Government of Rajasthan.
 
 
• The monument is well-preserved, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the region, despite being over two centuries old.

• Freedom to Reside and Settle in Any Part of the Territory of India, and

• This energy is stored in the form of **ATP **( Adenosine Triphosphate ) so, these are known as the "Powerhouse of the cell".

• **Ribosomes are present as free ribosomes in the cytoplasm or, as membrane-bound on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.**

• This phenomenon is a result of the increase in the kinetic energy of the air molecules.
 
• As the air molecules gain energy, they move more vigorously and spread out, leading to an increase in volume and expansion of the air.
 
• This expansion is commonly observed in various situations, such as hot air rising or the expansion of air in a balloon when it is exposed to heat.

**Statement II, which suggests that air becomes heavier on heating, is incorrect.**

 
• Heating air does not cause it to become heavier.
 
• In fact, as the air expands and occupies more space when heated, its density decreases, making it lighter compared to an equal volume of cooler air.
 
• This is why hot air tends to rise above cooler air in the atmosphere.

questions.question: In which of the soil conservation methods in the coastal and dry regions, rows of trees are planted to check the wind movement to protect soil cover?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shelter belts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shelter belts are rows of** trees and shrubs planted to protect soil from wind erosion, particularly in coastal and arid regions.**
 
• These tree lines reduce wind **speed across the ground and thereby decrease the wind's ability to lift and carry soil particles away, combating wind erosion effectively.**
 
• Apart from reducing **wind erosion, shelter belts also offer additional benefits like providing habitat for wildlife, sequestering carbon, and enhancing the landscape's aesthetics.**
 
• This method is quite common in **flat, dry regions where wind erosion is a major issue, such as parts of North America, Africa, and Asia.**
 
• Shelter belts can take the form of **single or multiple rows of trees or shrubs,** depending on the severity of the wind erosion problem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulching:**

 
 
• Mulching involves covering the soil surface with a layer of organic or inorganic material **(like straw, leaves, compost, or plastic sheets).**
 
• This technique **retains soil moisture, suppresses weed growth, and can also prevent soil erosion by reducing the impact of raindrops on the soil surface.**
 
 
 
• **Rock Dam:**
 
 
• Rock dams are barriers built across channels, gullies, or small waterways using rocks.
 
• They slow down the flow of water, reduce its erosive power and trap sediments.
 
• **This technique is commonly used in mountainous regions or areas prone to flash floods and gully erosion.**
 
 
 
• **Contour Barriers:**
 
 
• **​**Contour barriers are physical barriers like **stones, vegetation, or soil bunds constructed along the contours of a slope.**
 
• **They slow down water runoff, promote water infiltration, and reduce soil erosion by water.**
 
• This method is typically used on sloping land in both farming and forestry.
